author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Apple: Holiday Gifts - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Ever since Apple ( AAPL ) reported FQ4 results back on November 1, analysts have repeatedly come out negative on the stock. The company decided to quit reporting iPhone unit sales and the market hasn't stopped hammering the stock on feared sales weakness. One of the best ways to play analysts downgrading a stock in mass is to take a contrary view and the recent price cut of an ultra-bull is the likely signal that analysts are generally done cutting Apple targets.
Image Source: Apple website
Don't Follow The Herd The noticeable analyst action has been to repeatedly cut Apple's price target along with trimming EPS estimates. With the stock down below $170 now, the general view isn't actually that bearish.
Investors need to be careful that they don't get trapped with turning bearish on the stock due to a chorus of analysts repeatedly cutting estimates and targets for the same reason over and over.
The stock fell another 3.6% on Friday to $168 as ultra-bull analyst Katy Huberty cut her price target on Apple. The Morgan Stanley analyst has notably been one of the most bullish due to the company shifting into Services over the next five years.
The key here is that Ms. Huberty cut her price target to $236 from $253 and FY19 EPS estimate to $13.50 from $14.18. Based on an Asian trip, she became more concerned about iPhone replacement cycles in China and elsewhere in Asia.
Our recent meetings in Asia highlight a weakening China smartphone market, especially at the high-end where suppliers have seen order cuts across most vendors.
The key here is that her cut isn't actually new news. A whole herd of analysts have already cut targets due to lower than forecast iPhone sales. In fact, Bloomberg has the number of bulls (Buy ratings) at levels not seen since the financial crisis back prior to 2010.
Despite the stock down over $60 from the peak, analysts are actually less bullish on the stock than at any time in this decade. A funny thing happened Monday after yet another price target cut , Apple actually closed higher after an initial plunge.
Numbers Matter While all these cuts shift the sentiment, the more important measures are the actual numbers. Where are the consensus price targets and EPS estimates after all of these cuts.
According to yCharts data, EPS estimates have dipped from the highs back to start November. The FY19 and FY20 estimates are only down slightly from peak levels and FY21 estimates are currently up at $16.66.
AAPL EPS Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts
According to Yahoo! Finance, the FY19 EPS estimate was only $13.57 about 90 days ago. The numbers aren't that far different now.
Source: Yahoo! Finance
Even the average price target hasn't seen a big cut. Over the course of the last 3 months, the price target has only dipped about 3% to $226 now. The average target did peak near $240 and Appleinsider is using a $212 target so this data might not accurately capture some of the recent price target cuts.
Source: Seeking Alpha analyst ratings
Another clear indication of how analysts follow the herd was that the price targets were soaring into the quarterly results as Apple was about to pull the carpet out from under analysts. The stock hit a high of $233, but analysts pushed the price target up to $240 to stay one step ahead of the momentum.
Services To The Rescue While other investors are fretting the repeated negative news loop on iPhone sales, the smart move is to focus on Services growth and the stock buyback boost. My previous research detailed that 20%+ annualized Services growth over the next 5 years would generate $20 billion in additional gross profit while boosting the corporate gross margin by over 200 basis points.
Such a margin move was an inflection point in the last few years for the stocks of both Amazon ( AMZN ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ). In both cases, the tech giants moved to subscription services for that inflection. Now Microsoft trades at nearly double the forward P/E multiple of Apple.
AAPL PE Ratio (Forward 1y) data by YCharts
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that analysts are providing a holiday gift here. The stock trades at only 11.7x FY20 EPS estimates due to analysts constantly hitting Apple with the same issue over and over. All the while, the company is about to hit a margin inflection point that could finally lead to multiple expansion.
